subject: Math
title: EUS 3 · Expressions, Equations & Inequalities
source: C.A. Lyttle 2023 EUS study guide (merged_document.pdf / EUS7 Financial Literacy Highlights.pdf) — EUS 3 pp.7–10

lesson.title: GEMDAS
lesson.html: Grouping symbols → Exponents → Multiply/Divide (left to right) → Add/Subtract (left to right). It's a convention — you just memorize it.

lesson.title: Only like terms combine
lesson.html: 2x + 5x = 7x, but 2 + 5x can't combine. A variable by itself has a coefficient of 1.

lesson.title: 4 steps for a one-step equation
lesson.html: 1) Name the operation happening to the variable. 2) Name its inverse. 3) Apply the inverse to BOTH sides. 4) Check by plugging the answer back in.

lesson.title: Why it works
lesson.html: Identity property: do the SAME thing to both sides and nothing changes. Inverse property: opposites cancel.

lesson.title: Flip the sign!
lesson.html: When you multiply or divide both sides by a NEGATIVE number, flip the inequality symbol.

lesson.title: Graphing
lesson.html: Closed circle for ≥ or ≤ (included). Open circle for > or < (not included). A solid arrow shows all the solutions.

list.q: Why do expressions with variables have no solution?
list.a: Not enough information to know the variable's value
list.why: You can simplify an expression, but you can't solve it.

list.q: Why does the Order of Operations work the way it does?
list.a: It is a convention we all agreed on
w: It can be figured out with logic
list.why: It has to be memorized — you can't figure it out.

list.q: Why can you only combine LIKE terms?
list.a: Quantity only makes sense when it refers to something specific

list.q: What is the coefficient of x by itself?
list.why: A variable by itself still has a coefficient of 1.

list.q: What is Step 1 of solving a one-step equation?
list.a: Name the operation happening to the variable
list.why: First figure out what is being done to the variable.

list.a: Check by plugging the answer back in
list.why: Plug it back in and see if the equation is still true.

list.q: On a number line, the solution of an equation looks like…
w: An open circle with an arrow
list.why: An equation has one precise answer: one closed dot.

list.q: Doing the same thing to BOTH sides works because of the…
list.why: Identity: certain operations happen with “no change.”

list.q: When do you flip the inequality symbol?
list.a: When multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative
list.why: Multiplying/dividing by a negative turns both sides into their opposites.

list.q: An inequality's solution on a number line is…
list.a: An arrow with a circle at the start
The starting number is included (≥ or ≤)

list.q: Why must you be careful checking an inequality answer?
list.a: The answers are a whole set of numbers, not one
list.why: Plug in one number from the answer set to test it.
